name: BABYLON.IAccessibilityTag

doc: A string as alt text of the node, describing what the node is/does, for accessibility purpose.

name: BABYLON.IAccessibilityTag.eventHandler

name: BABYLON.IAccessibilityTag.role
doc: ARIA roles and attributes to customize accessibility support. If you use BabylonJS's accessibility html twin renderer, and want to override the default behavior (not suggested), this can be your way.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRControllerOptions
doc: Configuration options for the WebXR controller creation

name: BABYLON.IWebXRControllerOptions.disableMotionControllerAnimation
doc: Should the controller mesh be animated when a user interacts with it The pressed buttons / thumbstick and touchpad animations will be disabled

name: BABYLON.IWebXRControllerOptions.doNotLoadControllerMesh
doc: Do not load the controller mesh, in case a different mesh needs to be loaded.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRControllerOptions.forceControllerProfile
doc: Force a specific controller type for this controller. This can be used when creating your own profile or when testing different controllers

name: BABYLON.IWebXRControllerOptions.renderingGroupId
doc: Defines a rendering group ID for meshes that will be loaded. This is for the default controllers only.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRInputOptions
doc: The schema for initialization options of the XR Input class

name: BABYLON.IWebXRInputOptions.doNotLoadControllerMeshes
doc: If set to true no model will be automatically loaded

name: BABYLON.IWebXRInputOptions.forceInputProfile
doc: If set, this profile will be used for all controllers loaded (for example "microsoft-mixed-reality") If not found, the xr input profile data will be used. Profiles are defined here - https://github.com/immersive-web/webxr-input-profiles/

name: BABYLON.IWebXRInputOptions.disableOnlineControllerRepository
doc: Do not send a request to the controller repository to load the profile. Instead, use the controllers available in babylon itself.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRInputOptions.customControllersRepositoryURL
doc: A custom URL for the controllers repository

name: BABYLON.IWebXRInputOptions.disableControllerAnimation
doc: Should the controller model's components not move according to the user input

name: BABYLON.IWebXRInputOptions.controllerOptions
doc: Optional options to pass to the controller. Will be overridden by the Input options where applicable

name: BABYLON.IMotionControllerLayout.valueNodeProperty

doc: A definition for the layout map in the input profile

name: BABYLON.IMotionControllerProfile.fallbackProfileIds
doc: fallback profiles for this profileId

name: BABYLON.IMotionControllerProfile.layouts
doc: The layout map, with handedness as key

doc: The id of this profile correlates to the profile(s) in the xrInput.profiles array

doc: A helper-interface for the 3 meshes needed for controller button animation The meshes are provided to the _lerpButtonTransform function to calculate the current position of the value mesh

doc: the mesh that defines the pressed value mesh position. This is used to find the max-position of this button

doc: the mesh that defines the unpressed value mesh position. This is used to find the min (or initial) position of this button

name: BABYLON.IMotionControllerMeshMap.maxMesh
doc: the mesh that defines the maximum value mesh position.

name: BABYLON.IMotionControllerMeshMap.minMesh
doc: the mesh that defines the minimum value mesh position.

name: BABYLON.IMotionControllerMeshMap.valueMesh
doc: The mesh that will be changed when axis value changes

doc: The elements needed for change-detection of the gamepad objects in motion controllers

name: BABYLON.IMinimalMotionControllerObject.axes
doc: Available axes of this controller

name: BABYLON.IMinimalMotionControllerObject.buttons
doc: An array of available buttons

name: BABYLON.IMinimalMotionControllerObject.value
doc: Value of the button/trigger

name: BABYLON.IMinimalMotionControllerObject.touched
doc: If the button/trigger is currently touched

name: BABYLON.IMinimalMotionControllerObject.pressed
doc: If the button/trigger is currently pressed

doc: EXPERIMENTAL haptic support.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRWalkingLocomotionOptions
doc: Options for the walking locomotion feature.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRWalkingLocomotionOptions.locomotionTarget
doc: The target to be moved by walking locomotion. This should be the transform node which is the root of the XR space (i.e., the WebXRCamera's parent node).

name: BABYLON.IWebXRRawCameraAccessOptions
doc: Options for raw camera access

name: BABYLON.IWebXRRawCameraAccessOptions.doNotDisposeOnDetach
doc: Keep the created textures and metadata when detaching the feature.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRPlaneDetectorOptions
doc: Options used in the plane detector module

name: BABYLON.IWebXRPlaneDetectorOptions.worldParentNode
doc: The node to use to transform the local results to world coordinates

name: BABYLON.IWebXRPlaneDetectorOptions.doNotRemovePlanesOnSessionEnded
doc: If set to true a reference of the created planes will be kept until the next session starts If not defined, planes will be removed from the array when the feature is detached or the session ended.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRPlaneDetectorOptions.preferredDetectorOptions
doc: Preferred detector configuration, not all preferred options will be supported by all platforms.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRPlane
doc: A babylon interface for a WebXR plane. A Plane is actually a polygon, built from N points in space Supported in chrome 79, not supported in canary 81 ATM

name: BABYLON.IWebXRPlane.id
doc: a babylon-assigned ID for this polygon

name: BABYLON.IWebXRPlane.polygonDefinition
doc: an array of vector3 points in babylon space. right/left hand system is taken into account.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRPlane.transformationMatrix
doc: A transformation matrix to apply on the mesh that will be built using the polygonDefinition Local vs. World are decided if worldParentNode was provided or not in the options when constructing the module

name: BABYLON.IWebXRNearInteractionOptions
doc: Options interface for the near interaction module

name: BABYLON.IWebXRNearInteractionOptions.customUtilityLayerScene
doc: If provided, this scene will be used to render meshes.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRNearInteractionOptions.useUtilityLayer
doc: Should meshes created here be added to a utility layer or the main scene

name: BABYLON.IWebXRNearInteractionOptions.enableNearInteractionOnAllControllers
doc: Enable near interaction on all controllers instead of switching between them

name: BABYLON.IWebXRNearInteractionOptions.preferredHandedness
doc: The preferred hand to give the near interaction to. This will be prioritized when the controller initialize.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRNearInteractionOptions.disableSwitchOnClick
doc: Disable switching the near interaction from one controller to the other. If the preferred hand is set it will be fixed on this hand, and if not it will be fixed on the first controller added to the scene

name: BABYLON.IWebXRNearInteractionOptions.farInteractionFeature
doc: Far interaction feature to toggle when near interaction takes precedence

name: BABYLON.IWebXRNearInteractionOptions.nearInteractionControllerMode
doc: Near interaction mode for motion controllers

name: BABYLON.IWebXRNearInteractionOptions.motionControllerOrbMaterial
doc: Optional material for the motion controller orb, if enabled

name: BABYLON.IWebXRNearInteractionOptions.motionControllerTouchMaterialSnippetUrl
doc: If provided, this URL will be used by Node Material to generate the material for the motion controller orb If not provided, a snippet will be downloaded from the Babylon.js snippet server CDN. The NME JSON file can be found here - https://github.com/BabylonJS/Assets/blob/master/nme/nearInteractionTouchMaterial.json

name: BABYLON.IWebXRMeshDetectorOptions
doc: Options used in the mesh detector module

name: BABYLON.IWebXRMeshDetectorOptions.worldParentNode
doc: The node to use to transform the local results to world coordinates

name: BABYLON.IWebXRMeshDetectorOptions.doNotRemoveMeshesOnSessionEnded
doc: If set to true a reference of the created meshes will be kept until the next session starts If not defined, meshes will be removed from the array when the feature is detached or the session ended.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRMeshDetectorOptions.preferredDetectorOptions
doc: Preferred detector configuration, not all preferred options will be supported by all platforms. Babylon native only!

name: BABYLON.IWebXRMeshDetectorOptions.convertCoordinateSystems
doc: If set to true, WebXRMeshDetector will convert coordinate systems for meshes. If not defined, mesh conversions from right handed to left handed coordinate systems won't be conducted.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRMeshDetectorOptions.generateMeshes
doc: If set to true, the feature will generate meshes for the detected data. Note that this might be time consuming, as the mesh's vertex data will be updated on every change.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRVertexData
doc: A babylon interface for a XR mesh's vertex data.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRVertexData.id
doc: A babylon-assigned ID for this mesh

name: BABYLON.IWebXRVertexData.worldParentNode
doc: The node to use to transform the local results to world coordinates. WorldParentNode will only exist if it was declared in the IWebXRMeshDetectorOptions.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRVertexData.positions
doc: An array of vertex positions in babylon space. right/left hand system is taken into account.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRVertexData.indices
doc: An array of indices in babylon space. Indices have a counterclockwise winding order.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRVertexData.normals
doc: An array of vertex normals in babylon space. right/left hand system is taken into account.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRVertexData.transformationMatrix
doc: A transformation matrix to apply on the mesh that will be built using the meshDefinition. Local vs.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRVertexData.mesh
doc: If generateMeshes is set to true in the IWebXRMeshDetectorOptions, this will be the generated mesh. This mesh will be updated with the vertex data provided and not regenerated every time.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimationOptions
doc: Options for Light Estimation feature

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimationOptions.disableCubeMapReflection
doc: Disable the cube map reflection feature. In this case only light direction and color will be updated

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimationOptions.cubeMapPollInterval
doc: How often should the cubemap update in ms. If not set the cubemap will be updated every time the underlying system updates the environment texture.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimationOptions.lightEstimationPollInterval
doc: How often should the light estimation properties update in ms. If not set the light estimation properties will be updated on every frame (depending on the underlying system)

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimationOptions.createDirectionalLightSource
doc: Should a directional light source be created. If created, this light source will be updated whenever the light estimation values change

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimationOptions.reflectionFormat
doc: Define the format to be used for the light estimation texture.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimationOptions.disableVectorReuse
doc: Should the light estimation's needed vectors be constructed on each frame. Use this when you use those vectors and don't want their values to change outside of the light estimation feature

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimationOptions.disableSphericalPolynomial
doc: disable applying the spherical polynomial to the cube map texture

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimationOptions.disablePreFiltering
doc: disable prefiltering the cube map texture

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimation
doc: An interface describing the result of a light estimation

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimation.lightIntensity
doc: The intensity of the light source

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimation.lightColor
doc: Color of light source

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimation.lightDirection
doc: The direction from the light source

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLightEstimation.sphericalHarmonics
doc: Spherical harmonics coefficients of the light source

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLayersOptions
doc: Configuration options of the layers feature

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLayersOptions.preferMultiviewOnInit
doc: Whether to try initializing the base projection layer as a multiview render target, if multiview is supported. Defaults to false.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLayersOptions.projectionLayerInit
doc: Optional configuration for the base projection layer.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRImageTrackingOptions
doc: Options interface for the background remover plugin

name: BABYLON.IWebXRImageTrackingOptions.images
doc: A required array with images to track

name: BABYLON.IWebXRImageTrackingOptions.src
doc: The source of the image. can be a URL or an image bitmap

name: BABYLON.IWebXRImageTrackingOptions.estimatedRealWorldWidth
doc: The estimated width in the real world (in meters)

name: BABYLON.IWebXRTrackedImage
doc: An object representing an image tracked by the system

name: BABYLON.IWebXRTrackedImage.id
doc: The ID of this image (which is the same as the position in the array that was used to initialize the feature)

name: BABYLON.IWebXRTrackedImage.emulated
doc: Is the transformation provided emulated. If it is, the system "guesses" its real position.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRTrackedImage.originalBitmap
doc: Just in case it is needed - the image bitmap that is being tracked

name: BABYLON.IWebXRTrackedImage.realWorldWidth
doc: Width in real world (meters)

name: BABYLON.IWebXRTrackedImage.transformationMatrix
doc: A transformation matrix of this current image in the current reference space.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRTrackedImage.ratio
doc: The width/height ratio of this image. can be used to calculate the size of the detected object/image

name: BABYLON.IWebXRLegacyHitTestOptions.worldParentNode

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHitTestOptions

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHitTestOptions.disablePermanentHitTest
doc: Do not create a permanent hit test. Will usually be used when only transient inputs are needed.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHitTestOptions.enableTransientHitTest
doc: Enable transient (for example touch-based) hit test inspections

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHitTestOptions.transientHitTestProfile

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHitTestOptions.offsetRay

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHitTestOptions.transientOffsetRay

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHitTestOptions.entityTypes

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHitResult

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHitResult.inputSource

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHitResult.rotationQuaternion

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions
doc: Configuration interface for the hand tracking feature

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.jointMeshes
doc: Configuration object for the joint meshes.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.invisible
doc: Should the meshes created be invisible (defaults to false).

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.sourceMesh
doc: A source mesh to be used to create instances. Defaults to an icosphere with two subdivisions and smooth lighting.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.onHandJointMeshGenerated
sig: onHandJointMeshGenerated?: (meshInstance: InstancedMesh, jointId: number, hand: XRHandedness) => AbstractMesh | undefined

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.keepOriginalVisible
doc: Should the source mesh stay visible (defaults to false).

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.enablePhysics
doc: Should each instance have its own physics impostor

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.physicsProps
doc: If enabled, override default physics properties

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.scaleFactor
doc: Scale factor for all joint meshes (defaults to 1)

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.handMeshes
doc: Configuration object for the hand meshes.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.disableDefaultMeshes
doc: Should the default hand mesh be disabled. In this case, the spheres will be visible (unless set invisible).

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.customMeshes
doc: Rigged hand meshes that will be tracked to the user's hands. This will override the default hand mesh.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.meshesUseLeftHandedCoordinates
doc: Are the meshes prepared for a left-handed system. Default hand meshes are right-handed.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.customRigMappings
doc: If a hand mesh was provided, this array will define what axis will update which node. This will override the default hand mesh

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.customColors
doc: Override the colors of the hand meshes.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.disposeOnSessionEnd
doc: Define whether or not the hand meshes should be disposed on just invisible when the session ends. Not setting, or setting to false, will maintain the hand meshes in the scene after the session ends, which will allow q quicker re-entry into XR.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRHandTrackingOptions.disableHandShader
doc: Setting this will allow the developer to avoid loading the NME material and use the standard material instead.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRFeaturePoint
doc: A babylon interface for a "WebXR" feature point. Represents the position and confidence value of a given feature point.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRFeaturePoint.position
doc: Represents the position of the feature point in world space.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRFeaturePoint.confidenceValue
doc: Represents the confidence value of the feature point in world space. 0 being least confident, and 1 being most confident.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRDepthSensingOptions
doc: Options for Depth Sensing feature

name: BABYLON.IWebXRDepthSensingOptions.usagePreference
doc: The desired depth sensing usage for the session

name: BABYLON.IWebXRDepthSensingOptions.dataFormatPreference
doc: The desired depth sensing data format for the session

name: BABYLON.IWebXRDepthSensingOptions.disableDepthSensingOnMaterials
doc: Depth sensing will be enabled on all materials per default, if the GPU variant is enabled. If you just want to use the texture or the CPU variant instead set this to true.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRDepthSensingOptions.useToleranceFactorForDepthSensing
doc: If set to true the occluded pixels will not be discarded but the pixel color will be changed based on the occlusion factor Enabling this will lead to worse performance but slightly better outcome. It is possible we will change this in the future to look even better.

name: BABYLON.IWebXRDomOverlayOptions
doc: Options for DOM Overlay feature

name: BABYLON.IWebXRDomOverlayOptions.element

doc: Fluid color. Not used if generateDiffuseTexture is true

doc: Density of the fluid (positive number). The higher the value, the more opaque the fluid.

name: BABYLON.FluidRenderingTargetRenderer.refractionStrength
doc: Strength of the refraction (positive number, but generally between 0 and 0.3).

name: BABYLON.FluidRenderingTargetRenderer.fresnelClamp
doc: Strength of the fresnel effect (value between 0 and 1). Lower the value if you want to soften the specular effect

name: BABYLON.FluidRenderingTargetRenderer.specularPower
doc: Strength of the specular power (positive number). Increase the value to make the specular effect more concentrated

doc: Minimum thickness of the particles (positive number). If useFixedThickness is true, minimumThickness is the thickness used

name: BABYLON.FluidRenderingTargetRenderer.dirLight
doc: Direction of the light. The fluid is assumed to be lit by a directional light

doc: Gets or sets the feature (texture) to be debugged. Not used if debug is false

name: BABYLON.FluidRenderingTargetRenderer.debug
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if we should display a specific texture (given by debugFeature) for debugging purpose

name: BABYLON.FluidRenderingTargetRenderer.environmentMap
doc: Gets or sets the environment map used for the reflection part of the shading If null, no map will be used. If undefined, the scene.environmentMap will be used (if defined)

name: BABYLON.FluidRenderingTargetRenderer.enableBlurDepth
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating that the depth texture should be blurred

name: BABYLON.FluidRenderingTargetRenderer.blurDepthSizeDivisor
doc: Gets or sets the depth size divisor (positive number, generally between 1 and 4), which is used as a divisor when creating the texture used for blurring the depth For eg. if blurDepthSizeDivisor=2, the texture used to blur the depth will be half the size of the depth texture

name: BABYLON.FluidRenderingTargetRenderer.blurDepthFilterSize
doc: Size of the kernel used to filter the depth blur texture (positive number, generally between 1 and 20 - higher values will require more processing power from the GPU)

name: BABYLON.FluidRenderingTargetRenderer.blurDepthNumIterations
doc: Number of blurring iterations used to generate the depth blur texture (positive number, generally between 1 and 10 - higher values will require more processing power from the GPU)

name: BABYLON.FluidRenderingTargetRenderer.blurDepthMaxFilterSize
doc: Maximum size of the kernel used to blur the depth texture (positive number, generally between 1 and 200 - higher values will require more processing power from the GPU when the particles are larger on screen)

BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline
doc: The SSR rendering pipeline is used to generate a reflection based on a flat mirror model.

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.name
doc: Gets or sets the name of the rendering pipeline

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.isSSRSupported
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the SSR rendering pipeline is supported

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.maxDistance
doc: Gets or sets the maxDistance used to define how far we look for reflection during the ray-marching on the reflected ray (default: 1000). Note that this value is a view (camera) space distance (not pixels!).

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.step
doc: Gets or sets the step size used to iterate until the effect finds the color of the reflection's pixel. Should be an integer \>= 1 as it is the number of pixels we advance at each step (default: 1).

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.thickness
doc: Gets or sets the thickness value used as tolerance when computing the intersection between the reflected ray and the scene (default: 0.5). If setting "enableAutomaticThicknessComputation" to true, you can use lower values for "thickness" (even 0), as the geometry thickness is automatically computed thank to the regular depth buffer + the backface depth buffer

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.strength
doc: Gets or sets the current reflection strength. 1.0 is an ideal value but can be increased/decreased for particular results (default: 1).

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.reflectionSpecularFalloffExponent
doc: Gets or sets the falloff exponent used to compute the reflection strength. Higher values lead to fainter reflections (default: 1).

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.maxSteps
doc: Maximum number of steps during the ray marching process after which we consider an intersection could not be found (default: 1000). Should be an integer value.

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.roughnessFactor
doc: Gets or sets the factor applied when computing roughness. Default value is 0.2.

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.selfCollisionNumSkip
doc: Number of steps to skip at start when marching the ray to avoid self collisions (default: 1) 1 should normally be a good value, depending on the scene you may need to use a higher value (2 or 3)

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.reflectivityThreshold
doc: Gets or sets the minimum value for one of the reflectivity component of the material to consider it for SSR (default: 0.04). If all r/g/b components of the reflectivity is below or equal this value, the pixel will not be considered reflective and SSR won't be applied.

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.ssrDownsample
doc: Gets or sets the downsample factor used to reduce the size of the texture used to compute the SSR contribution (default: 0). Use 0 to render the SSR contribution at full resolution, 1 to render at half resolution, 2 to render at 1/3 resolution, etc.

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.blurDispersionStrength
doc: Gets or sets the blur dispersion strength. Set this value to 0 to disable blurring (default: 0.03) The reflections are blurred based on the roughness of the surface and the distance between the pixel shaded and the reflected pixel: the higher the distance the more blurry the reflection is.

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.blurDownsample
doc: Gets or sets the downsample factor used to reduce the size of the textures used to blur the reflection effect (default: 0). Use 0 to blur at full resolution, 1 to render at half resolution, 2 to render at 1/3 resolution, etc.

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.enableSmoothReflections
doc: Gets or sets whether or not smoothing reflections is enabled (default: false) Enabling smoothing will require more GPU power. Note that this setting has no effect if step = 1: it's only used if step \> 1.

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.attenuateScreenBorders
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the reflections should be attenuated at the screen borders (default: true).

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.attenuateIntersectionDistance
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the reflections should be attenuated according to the distance of the intersection (default: true).

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.attenuateIntersectionIterations
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the reflections should be attenuated according to the number of iterations performed to find the intersection (default: true).

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.attenuateFacingCamera
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the reflections should be attenuated when the reflection ray is facing the camera (the view direction) (default: false).

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.attenuateBackfaceReflection
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the backface reflections should be attenuated (default: false).

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.clipToFrustum
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the ray should be clipped to the frustum (default: true). You can try to set this parameter to false to save some performances: it may produce some artefacts in some cases, but generally they won't really be visible

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.useFresnel
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating whether the blending between the current color pixel and the reflection color should be done with a Fresnel coefficient (default: false). It is more physically accurate to use the Fresnel coefficient (otherwise it uses the reflectivity of the material for blending), but it is also more expensive when you use blur (when blurDispersionStrength \> 0).

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.enableAutomaticThicknessComputation
doc: Gets or sets a boolean defining if geometry thickness should be computed automatically (default: false). When enabled, a depth renderer is created which will render the back faces of the scene to a depth texture (meaning additional work for the GPU).

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.generateOutputInGammaSpace
doc: Gets or sets a boolean defining if the output color texture generated by the SSR pipeline should be in gamma space (default: true) If you have a post-process that comes after the SSR and that post-process needs the input to be in a linear space, you must disable generateOutputInGammaSpace

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.debug
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the effect should be rendered in debug mode (default: false). In this mode, colors have this meaning: - blue: the ray hit the max distance (we reached maxDistance) - red: the ray ran out of steps (we reached maxSteps) - yellow: the ray went off screen - green: the ray hit a surface.

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.camera
doc: Gets or sets the camera to use to render the reflection

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.useScreenspaceDepth
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the depth buffer stores screen space depth instead of camera view space depth.

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.normalsAreInWorldSpace
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the normals are in world space (false by default, meaning normals are in camera view space).

name: BABYLON.ThinSSRRenderingPipeline.normalsAreUnsigned
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the normals are encoded as unsigned, that is normalUnsigned = normal*0.5+0.5 (false by default).

doc:
Checks if all the post processes in the pipeline are ready.
@returns true if all the post processes in the pipeline are ready

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline
doc: Render pipeline to produce Screen Space Reflections (SSR) effect References: Screen Space Ray Tracing: - http://casual-effects.blogspot.com/2014/08/screen-space-ray-tracing.html - https://sourceforge.net/p/g3d/code/HEAD/tree/G3D10/data-files/shader/screenSpaceRayTrace.glsl - https://github.com/kode80/kode80SSR SSR: - general tips: https://sakibsaikia.github.io/graphics/2016/12/26/Screen-Space-Refl

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.SSRRenderEffect
doc: The SSR PostProcess effect id in the pipeline

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.SSRBlurRenderEffect
doc: The blur PostProcess effect id in the pipeline

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.SSRCombineRenderEffect
doc: The PostProcess effect id in the pipeline that combines the SSR-Blur output with the original scene color

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.samples
doc: MSAA sample count, setting this to 4 will provide 4x anti aliasing. (default: 1)

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.maxDistance
doc: Gets or sets the maxDistance used to define how far we look for reflection during the ray-marching on the reflected ray (default: 1000). Note that this value is a view (camera) space distance (not pixels!).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.step
doc: Gets or sets the step size used to iterate until the effect finds the color of the reflection's pixel. Should be an integer \>= 1 as it is the number of pixels we advance at each step (default: 1).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.thickness
doc: Gets or sets the thickness value used as tolerance when computing the intersection between the reflected ray and the scene (default: 0.5). If setting "enableAutomaticThicknessComputation" to true, you can use lower values for "thickness" (even 0), as the geometry thickness is automatically computed thank to the regular depth buffer + the backface depth buffer

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.strength
doc: Gets or sets the current reflection strength. 1.0 is an ideal value but can be increased/decreased for particular results (default: 1).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.reflectionSpecularFalloffExponent
doc: Gets or sets the falloff exponent used to compute the reflection strength. Higher values lead to fainter reflections (default: 1).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.maxSteps
doc: Maximum number of steps during the ray marching process after which we consider an intersection could not be found (default: 1000). Should be an integer value.

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.roughnessFactor
doc: Gets or sets the factor applied when computing roughness. Default value is 0.2.

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.selfCollisionNumSkip
doc: Number of steps to skip at start when marching the ray to avoid self collisions (default: 1) 1 should normally be a good value, depending on the scene you may need to use a higher value (2 or 3)

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.reflectivityThreshold
doc: Gets or sets the minimum value for one of the reflectivity component of the material to consider it for SSR (default: 0.04). If all r/g/b components of the reflectivity is below or equal this value, the pixel will not be considered reflective and SSR won't be applied.

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.ssrDownsample
doc: Gets or sets the downsample factor used to reduce the size of the texture used to compute the SSR contribution (default: 0). Use 0 to render the SSR contribution at full resolution, 1 to render at half resolution, 2 to render at 1/3 resolution, etc.

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.blurDispersionStrength
doc: Gets or sets the blur dispersion strength. Set this value to 0 to disable blurring (default: 0.03) The reflections are blurred based on the roughness of the surface and the distance between the pixel shaded and the reflected pixel: the higher the distance the more blurry the reflection is.

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.blurDownsample
doc: Gets or sets the downsample factor used to reduce the size of the textures used to blur the reflection effect (default: 0). Use 0 to blur at full resolution, 1 to render at half resolution, 2 to render at 1/3 resolution, etc.

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.enableSmoothReflections
doc: Gets or sets whether or not smoothing reflections is enabled (default: false) Enabling smoothing will require more GPU power. Note that this setting has no effect if step = 1: it's only used if step \> 1.

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.attenuateScreenBorders
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the reflections should be attenuated at the screen borders (default: true).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.attenuateIntersectionDistance
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the reflections should be attenuated according to the distance of the intersection (default: true).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.attenuateIntersectionIterations
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the reflections should be attenuated according to the number of iterations performed to find the intersection (default: true).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.attenuateFacingCamera
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the reflections should be attenuated when the reflection ray is facing the camera (the view direction) (default: false).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.attenuateBackfaceReflection
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the backface reflections should be attenuated (default: false).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.clipToFrustum
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the ray should be clipped to the frustum (default: true). You can try to set this parameter to false to save some performances: it may produce some artefacts in some cases, but generally they won't really be visible

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.useFresnel
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating whether the blending between the current color pixel and the reflection color should be done with a Fresnel coefficient (default: false). It is more physically accurate to use the Fresnel coefficient (otherwise it uses the reflectivity of the material for blending), but it is also more expensive when you use blur (when blurDispersionStrength \> 0).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.enableAutomaticThicknessComputation
doc: Gets or sets a boolean defining if geometry thickness should be computed automatically (default: false). When enabled, a depth renderer is created which will render the back faces of the scene to a depth texture (meaning additional work for the GPU).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.backfaceDepthRenderer
doc: Gets the depth renderer used to render the back faces of the scene to a depth texture.

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.backfaceForceDepthWriteTransparentMeshes
doc: Gets or sets a boolean (default: true) indicating if the depth of transparent meshes should be written to the backface depth texture (when automatic thickness computation is enabled).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.isEnabled
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the effect is enabled (default: true).

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.generateOutputInGammaSpace
doc: Gets or sets a boolean defining if the output color texture generated by the SSR pipeline should be in gamma space (default: true) If you have a post-process that comes after the SSR and that post-process needs the input to be in a linear space, you must disable generateOutputInGammaSpace

name: BABYLON.SSRRenderingPipeline.debug
doc: Gets or sets a boolean indicating if the effect should be rendered in debug mode (default: false). In this mode, colors have this meaning: - blue: the ray hit the max distance (we reached maxDistance) - red: the ray ran out of steps (we reached maxSteps) - yellow: the ray went off screen - green: the ray hit a surface.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.specularPower
doc: Defines how sharp are the highlights in the material. The bigger the value the sharper giving a more glossy feeling to the result.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.useEmissiveAsIllumination
doc: If true, the emissive value is added into the end result, otherwise it is multiplied in.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.linkEmissiveWithDiffuse
doc: If true, some kind of energy conservation will prevent the end result to be more than 1 by reducing the emissive level when the final color is close to one.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.useSpecularOverAlpha
doc: Specifies that the material will keep the specular highlights over a transparent surface (only the most luminous ones). A car glass is a good exemple of that.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.useReflectionOverAlpha
doc: Specifies that the material will keeps the reflection highlights over a transparent surface (only the most luminous ones). A car glass is a good exemple of that.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.disableLighting
doc: Does lights from the scene impacts this material. It can be a nice trick for performance to disable lighting on a fully emissive material.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.useObjectSpaceNormalMap
doc: Allows using an object space normal map (instead of tangent space).

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.useParallax
doc: Is parallax enabled or not.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.useParallaxOcclusion
doc: Is parallax occlusion enabled or not. If true, the outcome is way more realistic than traditional Parallax but you can expect a performance hit that worthes consideration.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.parallaxScaleBias
doc: Apply a scaling factor that determine which "depth" the height map should reprensent. A value between 0.05 and 0.1 is reasonnable in Parallax, you can reach 0.2 using Parallax Occlusion.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.roughness
doc: Helps to define how blurry the reflections should appears in the material.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.indexOfRefraction
doc: In case of refraction, define the value of the index of refraction.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.invertRefractionY
doc: Invert the refraction texture alongside the y axis. It can be useful with procedural textures or probe for instance.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.alphaCutOff
doc: Defines the alpha limits in alpha test mode.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.useLightmapAsShadowmap
doc: In case of light mapping, define whether the map contains light or shadow informations.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.diffuseFresnelParameters
doc: Define the diffuse fresnel parameters of the material.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.opacityFresnelParameters
doc: Define the opacity fresnel parameters of the material.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.reflectionFresnelParameters
doc: Define the reflection fresnel parameters of the material.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.refractionFresnelParameters
doc: Define the refraction fresnel parameters of the material.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.emissiveFresnelParameters
doc: Define the emissive fresnel parameters of the material.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.useReflectionFresnelFromSpecular
doc: If true automatically deducts the fresnels values from the material specularity.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.useGlossinessFromSpecularMapAlpha
doc: Defines if the glossiness/roughness of the material should be read from the specular map alpha channel

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.maxSimultaneousLights
doc: Defines the maximum number of lights that can be used in the material

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.invertNormalMapX
doc: If sets to true, x component of normal map value will invert (x = 1.0 - x).

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.invertNormalMapY
doc: If sets to true, y component of normal map value will invert (y = 1.0 - y).

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.twoSidedLighting
doc: If sets to true and backfaceCulling is false, normals will be flipped on the backside.

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.applyDecalMapAfterDetailMap
doc: If sets to true, the decal map will be applied after the detail map. Else, it is applied before (default: false)

name: BABYLON.StandardMaterial.prePassConfiguration
doc: Defines additional PrePass parameters for the material.

doc: Can this material render to prepass

doc: Can this material render to several textures at once

doc: Plugin that implements the sub surface component of the PBR material

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.DEFAULT_APPLY_ALBEDO_AFTERSUBSURFACE
doc: Default value used for applyAlbedoAfterSubSurface. This property only exists for backward compatibility reasons.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.DEFAULT_LEGACY_TRANSLUCENCY
doc: Default value used for legacyTranslucency. This property only exists for backward compatibility reasons.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.isRefractionEnabled
doc: Defines if the refraction is enabled in the material.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.isTranslucencyEnabled
doc: Defines if the translucency is enabled in the material.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.isDispersionEnabled
doc: Defines if dispersion is enabled in the material.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.isScatteringEnabled
doc: Defines if the sub surface scattering is enabled in the material.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.scatteringDiffusionProfile
doc: Diffusion profile for subsurface scattering. Useful for better scattering in the skins or foliages.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.refractionIntensity
doc: Defines the refraction intensity of the material. The refraction when enabled replaces the Diffuse part of the material.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.translucencyIntensity
doc: Defines the translucency intensity of the material. When translucency has been enabled, this defines how much of the "translucency" is added to the diffuse part of the material.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.useAlbedoToTintRefraction
doc: When enabled, transparent surfaces will be tinted with the albedo colour (independent of thickness)

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.useAlbedoToTintTranslucency
doc: When enabled, translucent surfaces will be tinted with the albedo colour (independent of thickness)

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.indexOfRefraction
doc: Index of refraction of the material base layer. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_refractive_indices This does not only impact refraction but also the Base F0 of Dielectric Materials.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.volumeIndexOfRefraction
doc: Index of refraction of the material's volume. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_refractive_indices This ONLY impacts refraction.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.invertRefractionY
doc: Controls if refraction needs to be inverted on Y. This could be useful for procedural texture.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.linkRefractionWithTransparency
doc: This parameters will make the material used its opacity to control how much it is refracting against not. Materials half opaque for instance using refraction could benefit from this control.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.minimumThickness
doc: Defines the minimum thickness stored in the thickness map. If no thickness map is defined, this value will be used to simulate thickness.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.maximumThickness
doc: Defines the maximum thickness stored in the thickness map.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.useThicknessAsDepth
doc: Defines that the thickness should be used as a measure of the depth volume.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.tintColor
doc: Defines the volume tint of the material. This is used for both translucency and scattering.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.tintColorAtDistance
doc: Defines the distance at which the tint color should be found in the media. This is used for refraction only.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.dispersion
doc: Defines the Abbe number for the volume.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.diffusionDistance
doc: Defines how far each channel transmit through the media. It is defined as a color to simplify it selection.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.translucencyColor
doc: Defines the translucency tint of the material. If not set, the tint color will be used instead.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.applyAlbedoAfterSubSurface
doc: This property only exists for backward compatibility reasons. Set it to true if your rendering in 8.0+ is different from that in 7 when you use sub-surface properties (transmission, refraction, etc.).

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.legacyTranslucency
doc: This property only exists for backward compatibility reasons. Set it to true if your rendering in 8.0+ is different from that in 7 when you use sub-surface translucency.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.legacyTransluceny
doc: Keeping for backward compatibility... Should not be used anymore.

name: BABYLON.PBRSubSurfaceConfiguration.isCompatible
doc:

@returns true if the plugin is compatible with the shader language

doc: Specifies the glossiness of the material. This indicates "how sharp is the reflection".

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessMaterial
doc: The PBR material of BJS following the metal roughness convention. This fits to the PBR convention in the GLTF definition: https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/blob/main/extensions/2.0/Archived/KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness/README.md

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessMaterial.baseColor
doc: The base color has two different interpretations depending on the value of metalness. When the material is a metal, the base color is the specific measured reflectance value at normal incidence (F0).

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessMaterial.metallic
doc: Specifies the metallic scalar value of the material. Can also be used to scale the metalness values of the metallic texture.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessMaterial.roughness
doc: Specifies the roughness scalar value of the material. Can also be used to scale the roughness values of the metallic texture.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial
doc: The Physically based material of BJS. This offers the main features of a standard PBR material.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.DEFAULT_AO_ON_ANALYTICAL_LIGHTS
doc: Defines the default value of how much AO map is occluding the analytical lights (point spot...).

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.directIntensity
doc: Intensity of the direct lights e.g. the four lights available in your scene.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.emissiveIntensity
doc: Intensity of the emissive part of the material. This helps controlling the emissive effect without modifying the emissive color.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.environmentIntensity
doc: Intensity of the environment e.g. how much the environment will light the object either through harmonics for rough material or through the reflection for shiny ones.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.specularIntensity
doc: This is a special control allowing the reduction of the specular highlights coming from the four lights of the scene. Those highlights may not be needed in full environment lighting.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.disableBumpMap
doc: Debug Control allowing disabling the bump map on this material.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.metallic
doc: Specifies the metallic scalar of the metallic/roughness workflow. Can also be used to scale the metalness values of the metallic texture.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.roughness
doc: Specifies the roughness scalar of the metallic/roughness workflow. Can also be used to scale the roughness values of the metallic texture.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.metallicF0Factor
doc: In metallic workflow, specifies an F0 factor to help configuring the material F0. By default the indexOfrefraction is used to compute F0; This is used as a factor against the default reflectance at normal incidence to tweak it.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.metallicReflectanceColor
doc: In metallic workflow, specifies an F0 color. By default the F90 is always 1; Please note that this factor is also used as a factor against the default reflectance at normal incidence.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.ambientColor
doc: The color of a material in ambient lighting.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.albedoColor
doc: AKA Diffuse Color in other nomenclature.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.baseWeight
doc: OpenPBR Base Weight (multiplier to the diffuse and metal lobes).

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.baseDiffuseRoughness
doc: OpenPBR Base Diffuse Roughness (roughness of the diffuse lobe).

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.reflectivityColor
doc: AKA Specular Color in other nomenclature.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.reflectionColor
doc: The color reflected from the material.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.emissiveColor
doc: The color emitted from the material.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.microSurface
doc: AKA Glossiness in other nomenclature.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.indexOfRefraction
doc: Index of refraction of the material base layer. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_refractive_indices This does not only impact refraction but also the Base F0 of Dielectric Materials.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.invertRefractionY
doc: Controls if refraction needs to be inverted on Y. This could be useful for procedural texture.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.linkRefractionWithTransparency
doc: This parameters will make the material used its opacity to control how much it is refracting against not. Materials half opaque for instance using refraction could benefit from this control.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useLightmapAsShadowmap
doc: If true, the light map contains occlusion information instead of lighting info.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.forceAlphaTest
doc: Enforces alpha test in opaque or blend mode in order to improve the performances of some situations.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.alphaCutOff
doc: Defines the alpha limits in alpha test mode.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useSpecularOverAlpha
doc: Specifies that the material will keep the specular highlights over a transparent surface (only the most luminous ones). A car glass is a good example of that.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useMicroSurfaceFromReflectivityMapAlpha
doc: Specifies if the reflectivity texture contains the glossiness information in its alpha channel.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useAmbientInGrayScale
doc: Specifies if the ambient texture contains the ambient occlusion information in its red channel only.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useAutoMicroSurfaceFromReflectivityMap
doc: In case the reflectivity map does not contain the microsurface information in its alpha channel, The material will try to infer what glossiness each pixel should be.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.usePhysicalLightFalloff
doc: BJS is using an hardcoded light falloff based on a manually sets up range. In PBR, one way to represents the falloff is to use the inverse squared root algorithm.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.usePhysicalLightFalloff
doc: BJS is using an hardcoded light falloff based on a manually sets up range. In PBR, one way to represents the falloff is to use the inverse squared root algorithm.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useGLTFLightFalloff
doc: In order to support the falloff compatibility with gltf, a special mode has been added to reproduce the gltf light falloff.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useGLTFLightFalloff
doc: In order to support the falloff compatibility with gltf, a special mode has been added to reproduce the gltf light falloff.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useRadianceOverAlpha
doc: Specifies that the material will keeps the reflection highlights over a transparent surface (only the most luminous ones). A car glass is a good example of that.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useObjectSpaceNormalMap
doc: Allows using an object space normal map (instead of tangent space).

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useParallax
doc: Allows using the bump map in parallax mode.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useParallaxOcclusion
doc: Allows using the bump map in parallax occlusion mode.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.parallaxScaleBias
doc: Controls the scale bias of the parallax mode.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.disableLighting
doc: If sets to true, disables all the lights affecting the material.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.forceIrradianceInFragment
doc: Force the shader to compute irradiance in the fragment shader in order to take bump in account.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.maxSimultaneousLights
doc: Number of Simultaneous lights allowed on the material.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.invertNormalMapX
doc: If sets to true, x component of normal map value will invert (x = 1.0 - x).

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.invertNormalMapY
doc: If sets to true, y component of normal map value will invert (y = 1.0 - y).

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.twoSidedLighting
doc: If sets to true and backfaceCulling is false, normals will be flipped on the backside.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useAlphaFresnel
doc: A fresnel is applied to the alpha of the model to ensure grazing angles edges are not alpha tested. And/Or occlude the blended part.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useLinearAlphaFresnel
doc: A fresnel is applied to the alpha of the model to ensure grazing angles edges are not alpha tested. And/Or occlude the blended part.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.forceNormalForward
doc: Force normal to face away from face.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.enableSpecularAntiAliasing
doc: Enables specular anti aliasing in the PBR shader. It will both interacts on the Geometry for analytical and IBL lighting.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useHorizonOcclusion
doc: This parameters will enable/disable Horizon occlusion to prevent normal maps to look shiny when the normal makes the reflect vector face the model (under horizon).

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.useRadianceOcclusion
doc: This parameters will enable/disable radiance occlusion by preventing the radiance to lit too much the area relying on ambient texture to define their ambient occlusion.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.unlit
doc: If set to true, no lighting calculations will be applied.

name: BABYLON.PBRMaterial.applyDecalMapAfterDetailMap
doc: If sets to true, the decal map will be applied after the detail map. Else, it is applied before (default: false)

name: BABYLON.PBRClearCoatConfiguration.intensity
doc: Defines the clear coat layer strength (between 0 and 1) it defaults to 1.

name: BABYLON.PBRClearCoatConfiguration.roughness
doc: Defines the clear coat layer roughness.

name: BABYLON.PBRClearCoatConfiguration.indexOfRefraction
doc: Defines the index of refraction of the clear coat. This defaults to 1.5 corresponding to a 0.04 f0 or a 4% reflectance at normal incidence The default fits with a polyurethane material.

name: BABYLON.PBRClearCoatConfiguration.remapF0OnInterfaceChange
doc: Defines if the F0 value should be remapped to account for the interface change in the material.

name: BABYLON.PBRClearCoatConfiguration.isTintEnabled
doc: Defines if the clear coat tint is enabled in the material.

name: BABYLON.PBRClearCoatConfiguration.tintColor
doc: Defines the clear coat tint of the material. This is only use if tint is enabled

name: BABYLON.PBRClearCoatConfiguration.tintColorAtDistance
doc: Defines the distance at which the tint color should be found in the clear coat media. This is only use if tint is enabled

name: BABYLON.PBRClearCoatConfiguration.tintThickness
doc: Defines the clear coat layer thickness. This is only use if tint is enabled

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial

doc: The Physically based material base class of BJS. This offers the main features of a standard PBR material.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial.DEFAULT_AO_ON_ANALYTICAL_LIGHTS
doc: Defines the default value of how much AO map is occluding the analytical lights (point spot...).

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial.ForceGLSL
doc: Force all the PBR materials to compile to glsl even on WebGPU engines. False by default.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._directIntensity
doc: Intensity of the direct lights e.g. the four lights available in your scene.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._emissiveIntensity
doc: Intensity of the emissive part of the material. This helps controlling the emissive effect without modifying the emissive color.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._environmentIntensity
doc: Intensity of the environment e.g. how much the environment will light the object either through harmonics for rough material or through the reflection for shiny ones.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._specularIntensity
doc: This is a special control allowing the reduction of the specular highlights coming from the four lights of the scene. Those highlights may not be needed in full environment lighting.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._disableBumpMap
doc: Debug Control allowing disabling the bump map on this material.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._metallic
doc: Specifies the metallic scalar of the metallic/roughness workflow. Can also be used to scale the metalness values of the metallic texture.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._roughness
doc: Specifies the roughness scalar of the metallic/roughness workflow. Can also be used to scale the roughness values of the metallic texture.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._metallicF0Factor
doc: In metallic workflow, specifies an F0 factor to help configuring the material F0. By default the indexOfrefraction is used to compute F0; This is used as a factor against the default reflectance at normal incidence to tweak it.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._metallicReflectanceColor
doc: In metallic workflow, specifies an F0 color. By default the F90 is always 1; Please note that this factor is also used as a factor against the default reflectance at normal incidence.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._ambientColor
doc: The color of a material in ambient lighting.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._albedoColor
doc: AKA Diffuse Color in other nomenclature.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._baseWeight
doc: Base Weight (multiplier to the diffuse and metal lobes).

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._baseDiffuseRoughness
doc: Base Diffuse Roughness (roughness of the diffuse lobe). Can also be used to scale the corresponding texture.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._reflectivityColor
doc: AKA Specular Color in other nomenclature.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._reflectionColor
doc: The color applied when light is reflected from a material.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._emissiveColor
doc: The color applied when light is emitted from a material.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._microSurface
doc: AKA Glossiness in other nomenclature.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._useLightmapAsShadowmap
doc: Specifies that the material will use the light map as a show map.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._useHorizonOcclusion
doc: This parameters will enable/disable Horizon occlusion to prevent normal maps to look shiny when the normal makes the reflect vector face the model (under horizon).

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._useRadianceOcclusion
doc: This parameters will enable/disable radiance occlusion by preventing the radiance to lit too much the area relying on ambient texture to define their ambient occlusion.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._useSpecularOverAlpha
doc: Specifies that the material will keeps the specular highlights over a transparent surface (only the most luminous ones). A car glass is a good example of that.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._useMicroSurfaceFromReflectivityMapAlpha
doc: Specifies if the reflectivity texture contains the glossiness information in its alpha channel.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._useAmbientInGrayScale
doc: Specifies if the ambient texture contains the ambient occlusion information in its red channel only.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._useAutoMicroSurfaceFromReflectivityMap
doc: In case the reflectivity map does not contain the microsurface information in its alpha channel, The material will try to infer what glossiness each pixel should be.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._lightFalloff
doc: Defines the falloff type used in this material. It by default is Physical.

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._useRadianceOverAlpha

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._useObjectSpaceNormalMap

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._useParallax

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._useParallaxOcclusion

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._invertNormalMapY

name: BABYLON.PBRBaseMaterial._alphaCutOff

doc:
Create a new ReflectionBlock
@param name defines the block name

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.directIntensity
doc: Intensity of the direct lights e.g. the four lights available in your scene.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.environmentIntensity
doc: Intensity of the environment e.g. how much the environment will light the object either through harmonics for rough material or through the reflection for shiny ones.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.specularIntensity
doc: This is a special control allowing the reduction of the specular highlights coming from the four lights of the scene. Those highlights may not be needed in full environment lighting.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.lightFalloff
doc: Defines the falloff type used in this material. It by default is Physical.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.useAlphaTest
doc: Specifies that alpha test should be used

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.alphaTestCutoff
doc: Defines the alpha limits in alpha test mode.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.useAlphaBlending
doc: Specifies that alpha blending should be used

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.useRadianceOverAlpha
doc: Specifies that the material will keeps the reflection highlights over a transparent surface (only the most luminous ones). A car glass is a good example of that.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.useSpecularOverAlpha
doc: Specifies that the material will keeps the specular highlights over a transparent surface (only the most luminous ones). A car glass is a good example of that.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.enableSpecularAntiAliasing
doc: Enables specular anti aliasing in the PBR shader. It will both interacts on the Geometry for analytical and IBL lighting.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.realTimeFiltering
doc: Enables realtime filtering on the texture.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.realTimeFilteringQuality
doc: Quality switch for realtime filtering

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.baseDiffuseModel
doc: Base Diffuse Model

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.useEnergyConservation
doc: Defines if the material uses energy conservation.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.useRadianceOcclusion
doc: This parameters will enable/disable radiance occlusion by preventing the radiance to lit too much the area relying on ambient texture to define their ambient occlusion.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.useHorizonOcclusion
doc: This parameters will enable/disable Horizon occlusion to prevent normal maps to look shiny when the normal makes the reflect vector face the model (under horizon).

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.unlit
doc: If set to true, no lighting calculations will be applied.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.forceNormalForward
doc: Force normal to face away from face.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.debugMode
doc: Defines the material debug mode. It helps seeing only some components of the material while troubleshooting.

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.debugLimit
doc: Specify from where on screen the debug mode should start. The value goes from -1 (full screen) to 1 (not visible) It helps with side by side comparison against the final render This defaults to 0

name: BABYLON.PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock.debugFactor
doc: As the default viewing range might not be enough (if the ambient is really small for instance) You can use the factor to better multiply the final value.

doc: Represents the different options available during the creation of a Environment helper. This can control the default ground, skybox and image processing setup of your scene.

doc: Specifies whether or not to create a ground. True by default.

doc: Specifies the ground size. 15 by default.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.groundColor
doc: The color mixed in the ground texture by default. BabylonJS clearColor by default.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.groundOpacity
doc: Specifies the ground opacity. 1 by default.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.enableGroundShadow
doc: Enables the ground to receive shadows. True by default.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.groundShadowLevel
doc: Helps preventing the shadow to be fully black on the ground. 0.5 by default.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.enableGroundMirror
doc: Creates a mirror texture attach to the ground. false by default.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.groundMirrorSizeRatio
doc: Specifies the ground mirror size ratio. 0.3 by default as the default kernel is 64.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.groundMirrorBlurKernel
doc: Specifies the ground mirror blur kernel size. 64 by default.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.groundMirrorAmount
doc: Specifies the ground mirror visibility amount. 1 by default

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.groundMirrorFresnelWeight
doc: Specifies the ground mirror reflectance weight. This uses the standard weight of the background material to setup the fresnel effect of the mirror.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.groundMirrorFallOffDistance
doc: Specifies the ground mirror Falloff distance. This can helps reducing the size of the reflection.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.groundYBias
doc: Specifies a bias applied to the ground vertical position to prevent z-fighting with the shown objects.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.createSkybox
doc: Specifies whether or not to create a skybox. True by default.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.skyboxSize
doc: Specifies the skybox size. 20 by default.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.skyboxColor
doc: The color mixed in the skybox texture by default. BabylonJS clearColor by default.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.backgroundYRotation
doc: The background rotation around the Y axis of the scene. This helps aligning the key lights of your scene with the background.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.sizeAuto
doc: Compute automatically the size of the elements to best fit with the scene.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.rootPosition
doc: Default position of the rootMesh if autoSize is not true.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.setupImageProcessing
doc: Sets up the image processing in the scene. true by default.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.cameraExposure
doc: The value of the exposure to apply to the scene. 0.6 by default if setupImageProcessing is true.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.cameraContrast
doc: The value of the contrast to apply to the scene. 1.6 by default if setupImageProcessing is true.

name: BABYLON.IEnvironmentHelperOptions.toneMappingEnabled
doc: Specifies whether or not tonemapping should be enabled in the scene. true by default if setupImageProcessing is true.

name: BABYLON.IMakeAnimationAdditiveOptions.range
doc: The name of the animation range to convert to additive. If not provided, fromFrame / toFrame will be used If fromFrame / toFrame are not provided either, the whole animation will be converted to additive

name: BABYLON.IMakeAnimationAdditiveOptions.cloneOriginalAnimation
doc: If true, the original animation will be cloned and converted to additive. If false, the original animation will be converted to additive (default is false)

name: BABYLON.IMakeAnimationAdditiveOptions.clonedAnimationName
doc: The name of the cloned animation if cloneOriginalAnimation is true. If not provided, use the original animation name

name: BABYLON.IMakeAnimationAdditiveOptions.fromFrame
doc: Together with toFrame, defines the range of the animation to convert to additive. Will only be used if range is not provided If range and fromFrame / toFrame are not provided, the whole animation will be converted to additive

name: BABYLON.IMakeAnimationAdditiveOptions.toFrame
doc: Together with fromFrame, defines the range of the animation to convert to additive.

name: BABYLON.IMakeAnimationAdditiveOptions.clipKeys
doc: If true, the key frames will be clipped to the range specified by range or fromFrame / toFrame (default is false)

name: GlobalEventHandlers.onbeforexrselect
sig: onbeforexrselect: ((this: GlobalEventHandlers, ev: XRSessionEvent) => any) | null
doc: An XRSessionEvent of type beforexrselect is dispatched on the DOM overlay element before generating a WebXR selectstart input event if the -Z axis of the input source's targetRaySpace intersects the DOM overlay element at the time the input device's primary action is triggered.

name: OffscreenCanvas.height
doc: These attributes return the dimensions of the OffscreenCanvas object's bitmap. They can be set, to replace the bitmap with a new, transparent black bitmap of the specified dimensions (effectively resizing it).

name: OffscreenCanvas.width
doc: These attributes return the dimensions of the OffscreenCanvas object's bitmap. They can be set, to replace the bitmap with a new, transparent black bitmap of the specified dimensions (effectively resizing it).

name: OffscreenCanvas.convertToBlob
doc: Returns a promise that will fulfill with a new Blob object representing a file containing the image in the OffscreenCanvas object. The argument, if provided, is a dictionary that controls the encoding options of the image file to be created.

name: OffscreenCanvas.getContext
doc: Returns an object that exposes an API for drawing on the OffscreenCanvas object. contextId specifies the desired API: "2d", "bitmaprenderer", "webgl", or "webgl2".
